transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, nice to meet you... what brings me in is, uh, I just always feel like I’ve got this motor humming under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like, if I'm in a staff meeting at the school where I work. Actually, they just bought these brand new floor buffers for the hallways, and let me tell you, you have to use a specific kind of wax or it leaves these terrible streaks, and the principal is real particular about the shine. He actually got on my case about it last Tuesday, which is ridiculous because I told him the supplier sent the wrong bucket... 

But anyway, yeah, in those meetings, or even during church event briefings—I help set up the fellowship hall on weekends—I just can't stay put. I end up shifting around in my chair the whole time, standing up in the back of the room, or just finding some excuse to go check the trash cans or something so I can move around. It just drives me crazy to just sit there.
Do you also often act without thinking first?

Act without thinking? Uh, no, I don't really think I do that. I actually try to plan things out. 

Like with the supply closet at the school, you really have to think ahead, especially with the heavy-duty trash bags. If you don't get the 55-gallon ones ordered by the first of the month, the cafeteria ladies just stuff the smaller ones until they split wide open. And let me tell you, cleaning up sloppy joes from the floor tile grout is an absolute nightmare. I actually had to use an old toothbrush on it a couple weeks ago because the sealant on the grout completely wore off near the serving line. My wife actually asked why I was packing a toothbrush in my lunchbox, and I had to explain to her that the district won't approve the budget for the industrial grout brushes... 

But, uh, wait. What were we talking about? Oh, doing things without thinking. Yeah, no, I haven't really noticed that. I'm usually pretty careful.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention when you need to focus?

Trouble focusing? No, I don't think so. When I need to get something done, I get it done. 

Like, uh, just yesterday I spent a solid two hours fixing the pneumatic closer on the main entrance door. You know those heavy commercial doors with the metal arms at the top? If you don't adjust the tension valve exactly right with an Allen wrench, the wind catches it and it slams so hard it rattles the glass in the front office. And the secretary, Brenda, she absolutely hates that. She’s got this whole collection of little ceramic frogs lined up on her desk—don't ask me why, I think her grandkids paint them or something—and a few months ago the door slammed and knocked one right off. Shattered everywhere. I had to get the special fine-dust attachment for the shop vac just to get all the little painted pieces out of the carpet fibers, because regular vacuums just spit that stuff right back out... 

But, uh, anyway. What was it you asked? Trouble paying attention? No, I don't have that problem. I can focus on whatever I'm working on just fine.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety even when you’re trying not to move?

Fidgety? Well, like I was saying about those staff meetings, I guess my legs just always want to bounce. Even when I'm just at home in my recliner trying to watch the evening news. 

It's one of those faux-leather ones, you know? Actually, the metal track on the footrest is starting to squeak really bad every time I shift my weight. I keep meaning to bring home some of the WD-40 Specialist spray from work—not the regular blue and yellow can, you gotta use the dry silicone one. People don't realize that regular WD-40 actually attracts dirt and ruins the tracks over time. They just spray it on door hinges and a month later it's a black, gummy mess. We had this guy, the new night shift guy, Gary, who went around spraying every single locker hinge in the boys' locker room with the regular stuff because he thought he was being helpful. It took me three days with an industrial citrus degreaser to fix it. And let me tell you, the smell of that orange degreaser, it just gets right up into your sinuses and lingers for a week. You can even taste it when you eat your sandwich at lunch... 

But, uh, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, feeling restless. I don't know, I just don't really like sitting still, I guess.
Do you often interrupt people or finish their sentences?

Interrupting people? Yeah, I guess I do that sometimes. It's just... well, like when my supervisor or one of the church staff starts telling me what they need done, I usually know exactly where they're going with it, so I just jump in and finish their sentence for them. Though, I guess sometimes I get it wrong and they have to correct me. 

Like last week, Pastor Dave was trying to tell me about setting up the folding chairs in the fellowship hall, and I just jumped in and said, "Yeah, yeah, 50 chairs in a semicircle, got it." But he was actually trying to tell me they needed the long banquet tables set up for a potluck. Have you ever tried to move those heavy wooden banquet tables by yourself? They're the old ones, solid core, probably weigh a hundred pounds each. You gotta lock the metal legs in just right or the whole thing collapses. We had one collapse during the Easter breakfast three years ago—scrambled eggs and little smokies everywhere. And let me tell you, getting dried egg off of industrial carpet is almost impossible. You have to use this special enzyme cleaner, and even then, if you don't extract it right away with the carpet machine, it leaves this weird yellowish stain that catches the light... 

But, uh, wait, what did you ask me? Interrupting? Yeah, I do jump in before people finish talking sometimes. I just want to get to work, you know?
